purpose: Replace hand-inserted capture with explicit enlarged systems in which visible orbital energy and momentum flow to a declared receiver, while preserving conservative focusing and static force amplification as mandatory null controls.

unit_system.synthetic: G=1 dimensionless encounter units except the c=1 weak-field GW fixture

mechanisms.capture_rule: A positive-energy orbit remains unbound; deflection is not capture.
A static attractive multiplier increases focusing but cannot turn a positive asymptotic energy into capture.
limits: time-independent A has no receiver flux

mechanisms.momentum_rule: equal-and-opposite collision impulse preserves total linear momentum
mechanisms.angular_momentum_rule: central contact impulse preserves orbital angular momentum; any off-axis torque enters receiver spin
mechanisms.capture_rule: true capture occurs only when E_orb_pre>0 and E_orb_post<0 with Q>0
limits: e=1 is the elastic no-dissipation limit
e=0 is maximum normal kinetic-energy loss

mechanisms.energy_rule: Delta_Q=K_rel_pre-K_rel_post for an impulse at fixed separation
mechanisms.capture_rule: the post-impulse orbital energy is evaluated without changing the gravitational potential
limits: the homogeneous Maxwellian approximation is not universal

mechanisms.momentum_rule: P_GW=0 for the frozen equal-mass symmetric quadrupole fixture
mechanisms.angular_momentum_rule: Delta_J_GW=6*pi*G^3*m1^2*m2^2/(c^5*r_p^2) in the parabolic weak-field approximation
mechanisms.entropy_rule: classical outgoing-wave coarse graining supplies an irreversible boundary condition; no microscopic thermodynamic entropy is asserted

mechanisms.energy_rule: Qdot=gamma0*h*|v1-v2|^2 and d(E_orb+Q)/dt=0 during the fixed-separation impulse
mechanisms.momentum_rule: F_receiver=-F_matter so total linear momentum is constant
mechanisms.capture_rule: capture can depend on earlier source activation at identical current r and v
limits: tau->infinity freezes the initial bath state

mechanisms.momentum_rule: equal-and-opposite receiver force preserves total linear momentum
mechanisms.angular_momentum_rule: receiver spin stores the negative orbital torque
mechanisms.entropy_rule: Sdot_receiver=Qdot/T_receiver>=0 for nonnegative weights, states and gamma0
mechanisms.capture_rule: a recent passage and an ancient passage produce separately testable fast and slow persistence tails
limits: w_s=0 reduces to the single-memory bath
both tau_i->0 reduce to instantaneous drag

mechanisms.momentum_rule: equal-and-opposite receiver force preserves total linear momentum
mechanisms.angular_momentum_rule: receiver spin stores the negative orbital torque
mechanisms.capture_rule: energy is removed on compression/infall but not on matched expansion/outflow

frozen_predictions: At fixed mass ratio, pericenter, gas fraction and pre-encounter structure, normalized integrated EnergyDissipation plus radiative cooling predicts a larger decrease in visible relative orbital energy and a shorter coalescence time.

At matched instantaneous separation, relative speed, mass ratio and gas fraction, post-pericenter systems have a larger residual loss rate than first-infall systems only for a memory bath; an instantaneous shock law has no history residual after its measured gas state is controlled.

The bimodal bath predicts a fast approximately one-Gyr decay and a distinct slow persistence tail in phase-space distance; the frozen constants are calibrated only to the published one-object Illustris benchmark and must be tested without retuning on TNG100-1.
Any visible orbital angular-momentum deficit must be balanced by gas/internal spin, outflow or radiative flux within the declared aperture ledger.

A matched TNG100-1-Dark history can show collisionless mixing and clumping without positive gas receiver flux; morphology or phase-space persistence alone is therefore insufficient evidence for dissipation.

The candidate must outperform Newtonian time-dependent collisionless evolution, standard shock/cooling, the Boylan-Kolchin extended-satellite merger-time law, dissipative-DM cooling/gravothermal-collapse models, and flexible history controls before a new-gravity interpretation is considered.

observations: phase-space mixing distance falls by about 80 percent during the first 1 Gyr after the merger
the remaining distance falls by about 50 percent over the following 8.5 Gyr
published_benchmark.use: calibrate a two-mode persistence control only; do not claim prediction or independent confirmation

ranking_policy.dual_grade_rule: data fit and theory health remain separate; a theory tension cannot be relabeled as a data rejection
